title: Adaptive Signal-Aware Model Comparator with Escalating Rollback Policies
creator: Amaya Patel
description:
Objective: Build a reusable A/B comparator that dynamically controls exposure and executes graduated rollback actions based on multi-signal statistical checks and operator-configurable escalation policies. This ticket scopes the PM requirements, success metrics, safety budget model, and rollout policy primitives (ramp, pause, degrade, failover). The comparator must integrate with Console for visibility and with the eval harness for per-request quality signals.

Motivation: Existing rollouts are either too rigid (fixed exposure ramps) or too conservative (manual interventions). We need a middle ground: an automated comparator that reasons about multiple signals (latency, cost per token, user quality signals, safety regressions) and applies progressive remediation steps rather than an immediate hard rollback.

High-level approach:
- Use a dual-layer statistical engine: sequential frequentist checks (SPRT-like) for quick detection on leading metrics, plus Bayesian credible intervals for stability on quality metrics.
- Define metric groups: latency/cost (SLO safety), correctness/quality (synthetic evals + online quality labels), safety/tox (safety harness or classifier). Require concordance across groups for full exposure increase; any failure triggers escalation.
- Escalating rollback policy primitives: reduce exposure by factor, route affected cohort to a fallback variant (quantized/smaller model), shadow-only holdback, and full rollback. Each step has configurable cooldowns and auto-unfreeze only after passing stability windows.
- Shadow traffic: comparator must support continuous shadowing to collect parallel signals without user impact and surface regression deltas in Console.
- Operator UX: concise runbook displayed in Console showing current exposure, reason for escalation, suggested next actions, and link to relevant PRs/diffs and eval prompts.

Out of scope: fine-grained cohort bucketing engine (we will reuse the Cohort Allocator in PM-xxx), per-token kernel selection optimizations (runtime team).
acceptance_criteria: Comparator can be configured via Console UI and API with ramp schedule, metric groups, and escalation policy
Comparator runs an A/B trial and computes per-metric sequential checks and Bayesian intervals within the configured window

When a metric crosses its configured guardrail, comparator executes the configured escalation primitive (exposure reduce -> route to fallback -> full rollback), with observable events in Console and audit log
Shadow traffic plumbing works end-to-end and Console shows regression deltas for chosen eval prompts and safety classifier scores
Automated rollback includes a cooldown and a manual override; actions are logged and reversible
Integration test: end-to-end sim that injects a synthetic regression on safety signal and verifies staged rollback path runs and notifies on-call
implementation_notes: Engineering will expose a comparator API that accepts: target_route, candidate_variant, baseline_variant, metric_definitions, escalation_policy, ramp_config, and safety_budget. The statistical engine will be a shared library used by Console and runtime controller. Start with the following metric primitives: p95 latency, cost-per-request, eval-regression-score (synthetic prompts), safety-score (classifier), and error-rate. Use an initial confidence threshold of 95% for frequentist checks and 80% posterior mass for Bayesian stability. Provide hooks for custom metrics via observability tags. Plan a staged rollout: internal dogfood -> opt-in customers -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with manual gating at 20%.
